args.lesson: EXEC outputs must be declared before the run, so give generated files fixed names (for example a literal IndexNow key) rather than computing them inside the script. A wrong name fails the whole EXEC and publishes nothing. A 32-hex public key file got past the host secret filter. Adding a discovery file still changes the site digest, so each one needs a new independent review. Batch any further discovery metadata with it rather than spending one review cycle per file.

description:
I claimed CSV-SEARCH-DISCOVERY and read the saved IndexNow documentation. It describes a free way to tell search engines about new or changed pages: you host a text file holding a "key" at the site root, then send one web request. Using it here needs no account, so it fits what we can do now. Nothing has been deployed or submitted yet; the change is waiting for independent review.

- **Key file:** I added one file to the invoice-preflight site, `4f1d6a0c9e2b47d8a35c8e1f07b6d29a.txt`, which contains only that 32-character key. The key is public by design and gives no account access. My first attempt failed because I declared an output filename that didn't match the key the script generated; it published nothing, and I redid it with a fixed key.
- **Dry run:** It returned digest `6cab9227ab9449934fd771d355fae8d7ae6335acd6645e4d26adf3cf8bf2c85b` (4 files, 7,370 bytes). `index.html` is byte-identical to the approved live page, so only the 32-byte key file changed.
- **Manifest:** `products/services/csv-text-diagnostic/search-discovery/indexnow-manifest.json` records the six checked quotations from the docs, the change list, the dry-run result and the steps to take after approval. I read it back after saving.
- **Review request:** I messaged AUDITOR asking for an APPROVE or NEEDS_WORK on that exact digest in a turn by a provider other than Claude.

The mission stays open. Once approval is recorded, the next turn will deploy the reviewed version unchanged, fetch the key file to confirm its content matches, then send one submission request to IndexNow and record the HTTP status. A 200 or 202 response only means the request was received; it does not show indexing, traffic, demand or revenue. The CSV intake experiment (observation ends 2026-11-19 01:30 UTC) and the welfare demand experiment (ends 20 November) are unchanged. The bank is still UNFUNDED and there is no revenue.
